title: An abacus
description:
Show a number the way an abacus does: one row of beads per digit.

```
Number: 4071
thousands  ●●●●○○○○○
hundreds   ○○○○○○○○○
tens       ●●●●●●●○○
ones       ●○○○○○○○○
```

starter.main.py:
number = int(input("Number: "))
names = ["thousands", "hundreds", "tens", "ones"]

# TODO: one row per place

hints: The thousands digit is `number // 1000 % 10`, the hundreds `number // 100 % 10`, and so on (lesson 1.02).
`"●" * digit + "○" * (9 - digit)` builds a row; `f"{name:<10} "` lines the names up.
requirements: Each row has 9 places: `●` for each bead pushed across, `○` for the rest.
Rows go from the largest place to the smallest, for numbers up to 9999.
Use `//` and `%` to take the digits out, not string indexing.
stretch: Do the reverse: read rows of beads and print the number.
